Subject: Urgent: sudden spike in 5xx/429s for our dedicated pool

Hi Naomi,

Starting ~07:50 PST we began seeing a large increase in 5xx and 429 responses from the Redwood dedicated endpoints (region: us-west-2) for our /v1/generate routes. Throughput dropped and many requests timed out — our retries look to have amplified the problem. We attached logs and a short pcap from an affected host.

Symptoms:
- 5xx and 429 rate jumped from ~0.2% to ~18%
- Clients experience 1.5s additional tail latency before retries
- Large number of TCP retransmits and duplicated SYNs in pcap

This is hitting our checkout path so it’s P0. Can you confirm if there are known issues on Redwood’s end (peering/NAT/firewall) or anything we should change? We can open a call.

Subject: Fwd: SignalWave 5xx spike - attaching logs/pcap from customer

Forwarding Aisha's message and attachments. Quick summary from my side after an initial glance at their logs: 429/5xx pattern plus heavy retransmit -> looks like retry amplification tied to SNAT port exhaustion or aggressive firewall idle timeouts on SignalWave side. They are on a Dedicated pool with VPC peering to our infra.

Why this matters: if a customer-side NAT runs out of ephemeral ports, retries can cause many connections to be queued and reset causing elevated 5xxs at our edge. Conversely, asymmetric NAT translations or short TCP timeout on their firewall can produce half-open flows that our backend sees as failures and retries.

Asks for Jonas (on-call infra): can you prioritize digging into the peering NAT metrics and our egress behaviour for this customer's namespace? Also suggest we consider a short-term circuit-breaker on the route and reduce client-side retries for this customer until we confirm root cause.

--- Forwarded message ---
""
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: SignalWave 5xx spike - attaching logs/pcap from customer

Thanks — I dug into the captures and our telemetry. Quick findings: 
- PCAP shows many duplicated SYNs and multiple retransmissions from a small pool of client IPs.
- On our side, the dedicated peering path is healthy (no packet drops at the core), but we see a sudden concentration of ephemeral port reuse from SignalWave's NAT range.
- Cloud provider NAT metrics (shared via their console) indicate SNAT port utilization ~98% at the time of the surge.

Interpretation: the signal is consistent with SNAT port exhaustion at the customer side. When their hosts exhaust ephemeral ports, they retry aggressively; this causes our front-end connections to be reset or delayed, producing 5xx and 429 behavior on both sides (their retries translated into heavy concurrent flows).

Recommended immediate mitigations (short-term):
1) Ask SignalWave to expand ephemeral port range / increase NAT capacity and raise firewall connection tracking limits.
2) Have Redwood apply a per-connection circuit-breaker for that namespace: limit inflight requests to their tenant to avoid further amplification (we can do this for a short window).
3) Disable aggressive client-side retries via an API-config flag if they can tweak their SDK quickly.
4) If firewall idle-timeout < 300s, increase to avoid premature connection teardown.

I’ve attached my packet notes in the ticket. If they can make the config changes, I expect the 5xx/429 rate to fall within ~10-20 minutes after their NAT pressure subsides.

Jonas
SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>

- Customer SignalWave (Strategic, $1.2M ARR) is experiencing a P0 impacting checkout. Root cause appears to be SNAT port exhaustion / firewall config on their side that is triggering retry amplification.
- Customer is requesting 24/7 L3 coordination and potential SLA credit/waiver given production impact.

Asks: 
1) Approve immediate L3 engagement and cover up to 8 hours of dedicated on-call support (we can convert to billable later) — request approval for up to $5k in support credits if needed.

3) If legal needs to be looped for an SLA exception, please flag.

We have an action plan: Jonas will coordinate infra mitigations, Marissa will coordinate CS touchpoints, Rishi will own account comms. I’m standing by to run the customer call.

—Naomi

From: James Li <james.li@signalwave.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@signalwave.ai>, support@signalwave.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 12:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SignalWave dedicated pool outage - we’re applying NAT adjustments now

Naomi — thanks for the quick help and the suggested mitigations. We pushed the following at 12:15 PST:
- Increased SNAT pool size and expanded ephemeral port range on our NAT gateway
- Raised firewall conntrack timeout from 60s -> 600s
- Temporarily dialed down client retry backoff in our SDK (1.5x -> 1.1x)

Preliminary metrics show errors dropping back toward baseline; we’ll send a post-fix pcap and logs in ~30 minutes. We appreciate the offer of L3 support and will take you up on a short postmortem call this afternoon.

Thanks,
James
CTO, SignalWave
